subject: Q&A is there a way for mlg.id to ignore NA and/or allow for x mismatches?

messages.author: 0e3530e13131a3d4
messages.subject: Q&A is there a way for mlg.id to ignore NA and/or allow for x mismatches?
parts:
Hi everyone,

I have used the mlg.id function to identify individuals that were sampled multiple times (duplicates in the data) in the following way:

cloned_gt <- mlg.id(df)

duplicates <- cloned_gt[which(lengths(cloned_gt)>1)]

But this will only find exact matches. Is there a way to ignore NAs in the data? So that for example genotype A B C D and genotype A B NA D would be considered a match?

In addition to this, would it be possible to allow for 1 (or more) mismatches? So that genotype A B C D would be considered a match with A B E D?

Any help would be greatly appreciated!

All the best,
Anneke

messages.author: c9df9e12efe33730
messages.subject: Re: Q&A is there a way for mlg.id to ignore NA and/or allow for x mismatches?
parts:
Hi Anneke,

All of what you are asking is indeed possible in poppr! I would suggest you read the "mlg" poppr vignette. You can access it by typing in the R console:

```
library(poppr)
vignette(topic = "mlg", package = "poppr")
```

I will use the monpop dataset which is included with poppr to quickly demonstrate how you can do what you are asking (but you should definitely also read the appropriate vignette in order to see all options and understand the topic)
Is there a way to ignore NAs in the data?

All we need to do is use the mlg.filter function with a genetic distance of our choice. I will use the diss.dist function to calculate distances between genotypes, as it has the desired property that each unit is equal to one allele difference. By setting the distance threshold for separating genotypes to 0 + a very tiny number, poppr will ignore missing data and consider individuals with the same genotype apart from missing data as matches.

```
data(monpop)
mlg.filter(monpop, distance = diss.dist) <- 0 + .Machine$double.eps^0.5
monpop
```

Similarly if you would like to allow 1 missmatch (or more), all you have to do is supply the appropriate distance threshold:

```
mlg.filter(monpop, distance = diss.dist) <- 1 + .Machine$double.eps^0.5
monpop
```

Hope this helps
Nikos
